newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First, Lab caucuses meet, National's postponed.
newsitem.headline: NZ First, Lab caucuses meet, National's postponed.

text.p: The Labour and New Zealand First parties went into caucus meetings on Tuesday morning but neither would consider a final coalition document today, party sources said.
The conservative National Party caucus pencilled in for Tuesday has been postponed, a spokeswoman for caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger said.

"We normally do have a caucus on Tuesday. There was one pencilled in today but it has been decided not to have it. It will be held when necessary but there is not a date pencilled in yet," the spokeswoman said.
She said no times had been set for any further formal talks with NZ First.
She said paper work and reports had been exchanged by facsimile and telephone between National and NZ First since last Friday.
Nationalist NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is holding talks with centre-left Labour and conservative National over the shape of the next government.
An NZ First MP told Reuters before Tuesday's caucus meeting a deal was very close but would not be struck today.
The MP said almost all the paper work had been completed and the party would soon be in a position to decide who it would join in a coalition.
"The paperwork is complete or, if it isn't, then 98 percent complete," the MP said.
"A deal is close, and that is not speculation."
